sections.text_helper: Section 73.12 "OTG interrupts" in chapter 73 (USB on-the-go high-speed (OTG)), RM0486 Rev 4, page 3780.
sections.section_content:
When the OTG controller is operating in one mode, either device or host, the application
must not access registers from the other mode. If an illegal access occurs, a mode
mismatch interrupt is generated and reflected in the core interrupt register (MMIS bit in the
OTG_GINTSTS register). When the core switches from one mode to the other, the registers
in the new mode of operation must be reprogrammed as they would be after a power-on
reset.
Figure990 shows the interrupt hierarchy.
[Figure 990. Interrupt hierarchy]
1. OTG_WKUP becomes active (high state) when resume condition occurs during L1 SLEEP or L2 SUSPEND states.
